source.title: Decompose Sparsely Where You Should, Absorb Densely Where You Should No
source.authors: Rui-Xuan Deng; Ze-Hao Jin; Ze-Kun Wang; Zi-Han Dong

record.file_problem: Complete paper text is present. Some figure and table material is garbled in the web extraction, but the main text and relevant numerical tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAE probes, feature ablations, and causal interventions in a language model to test how well sparse dictionaries represent activation content. This is a different method and setting from the toy-model superposition claim, and it bears on V4 and the completeness aspect of V5.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses Toy Models of Superposition as background and says the relation of its dense scaffold to that framework is an open question; it does not test the toy-model overlap geometry or a sparsity-dependent transition. Rows record its own Gemma-2-2B results on sparse-code probing, dense latents, topic information, and interventions. Cited findings from other work and unreported or figure-only numerical details are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: On Gemma-2-2B layer 12, the paper argues with ablation results that standard SAE dictionaries do not hold the residual stream's low-rank, causally critical component as discrete sparse units. Ablating 787 scaffold-aligned SAE features raises CE to 5.5, versus 14.3 when the 24-d component is removed. Ablating 2,048 topic-aligned atoms leaves topic accuracy above 99%. This is an argument that V5 (dictionary features as the model's units) needs restating. The bottleneck-vs-no-bottleneck benchmark gains compare the paper's own method with the standard SAE and do not test V4. TMS geometry (V1) is only discussed as an open question.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress that sparse dictionaries encode the scaffold redundantly, not compactly. They say it is a shared source of persistent dense latents, and that the most causally important structure may be what SAEs handle least well.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds a trained low-rank linear bottleneck parallel to BatchTopK or Matryoshka SAEs and measures representational and causal effects; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method or its toy-network feature-geometry experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with bottleneck rank and SAE architecture. Rank 24 reduces dense latent counts; at rank 2304 the bottleneck starves the SAE. The paper also reports architecture-dependent effects for some SAE metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: A rank-24 dense component, aligned with the top principal components and outlier dimensions, is causally critical (CE 1.90→14.3) and absorbs the dense latents that SAEs otherwise form. The authors call it unlike any feature TMS considers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM residual streams contain a low-rank dense scaffold outside the sparse-superposition picture, and it is a source of SAE dense latents.

record.problems: The experiments use a single model and layer, as the authors acknowledge. The text reports no error bars or confidence intervals for the listed results. Some rank-sweep values are tabulated, while several figure values are not numerically reported.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted additional SAE benchmark metrics not directly bearing on V4 or V5 (including SCR, RAVEL, and autointerp), as well as detailed appendix analyses of sentiment, Matryoshka groups, and dense-latent categories. Figure-only numerical values for the rank curve, dose-response, and feature-ablation curves were not extracted where the text gave no corresponding number.

untested.parts: No toy networks, overlap geometry or sparsity transition. TMS is discussed only as an open question about the scaffold.
Assumed rather than tested. SAE benchmark scores are reported only as differences between the paper's bottleneck and a plain SAE.
Stability across seeds and canonicality are not tested. Only one model and layer (Gemma-2-2B L12) and only residual-stream SAEs are studied.
Not tested as such. The scaffold is a 24-d dense component with topic spread across its dimensions, but it is not framed as a multi-dimensional feature.

missing.what: In the baseline BatchTopK SAE, 25 of 25 dense latents align with the scaffold (α>0.3) and only 7 of 25 are classifiable. 787 features align with the outlier component, falling to 99 at r=24.
Which SAE (r=0 or r=24, BatchTopK or Matryoshka) was used for the 787-feature and 2,048-atom ablations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 labels rest on comparisons between the paper's method and a plain SAE, so they are dropped; V4 is assumed, not tested. The V5 label is limits_scope rather than challenges: the sparse code still contains the scaffold's information (98–99.8% topic accuracy, 96% subspace coverage). It just does not localize it in tractable units. Only one model and layer is tested, with no error bars. The scaffold-removal effect is replicated across two bottleneck architectures.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, their overlap geometry, or a sparsity-dependent transition.
It does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by feature competition for capacity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Tests SAE feature recovery and distributed representation of selected content in Gemma-2-2B layer 12; it does not test feature spread across neurons generally, other models, or other layers.

Tests whether the sparse dictionary efficiently and completely represents the measured scaffold and topic information. It does not test feature stability across seeds or whether SAE features are canonical units generally.
The study identifies a 24-dimensional scaffold subspace but does not test whether individual superposed features are one-dimensional versus multidimensional.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12, 16k-latent SAE at L0=40; low-rank top-variance (scaffold) content
relationships.reason: The SAE features cover the scaffold geometrically, yet ablating them only partly reproduces its causal effect (R19: CE 5.5 vs 14.3 in R15/R16). Ablating 2,048 topic atoms leaves accuracy above 99%, while scaffold ablation gives chance (R13 vs R12). So dictionary units are not the model's units for this content.
relationships.display_finding: Ablating SAE features that geometrically covered the scaffold gave CE 5.5 versus 14.3 for ablating the scaffold itself, and removing 2,048 topic atoms left accuracy above 99% while scaffold ablation dropped it to chance.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12, 16k-latent SAE at L0=40; low-rank top-variance (scaffold) content
source_check.reason: R19 shows a substantial but incomplete causal effect despite 96% geometric coverage; R13 retains above-99% topic accuracy after extensive sparse ablation, unlike R12. These results qualify dictionary-unit completeness for scaffold content; stability and canonicity remain untested.

labels.reason: R19 shows a substantial but incomplete causal effect despite 96% geometric coverage; R13 retains above-99% topic accuracy after extensive sparse ablation, unlike R12. These results qualify dictionary-unit completeness for scaffold content; stability and canonicity remain untested.

relation.reason: Its own interventions test whether SAE dictionary features compactly capture the scaffold's information and causal role.

tranche.reason: The study directly argues, using causal and topic-probe ablations, that full sparse decomposability needs qualifying for low-rank scaffold content.

source_check.notes: Results concern one model and layer. Section 5.3 does not explicitly identify whether its ablated SAE is r=0 or r=24; its multinomial topic-probe baselines differ from the binary OvR results.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12, BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs at L0=40; tested sparse probes and targeted probe perturbation
reader_labels.reason: Sparse-code probe accuracy and TPP improve with the bottleneck in both SAE architectures, showing that SAE features recover and can perturb measured information in this setting (R1-R3, R5-R7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12; scaffold and topic-information measurements
reader_labels.reason: A compact bottleneck carries topic information and removing it strongly disrupts next-token prediction, while sparse-feature ablation does not reproduce that causal effect; this limits the claim that sparse features capture the model's relevant representation broadly (R9-R19).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12; scaffold and MMLU topic-information tests
reader_labels.reason: The study reports that a compact bottleneck captures topic information and is causally important, while aligned sparse-feature ablations leave substantial topic accuracy and do not reproduce the scaffold-removal effect; this challenges completeness of the sparse dictionary for the tested content, but does not test stability or canonicality generally (R11-R19).
